rows.title: ECG Rhythm Conduction Ptbxl
rows.summary: Variant ptbxl 2263: Single PTB XL derived rhythm/conduction benchmark slice with 2,263 anonymized ECG records.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a computational precision health researcher working on staged ECG waveform data.

## Variant
`ptbxl_2263`: Single PTB-XL-derived rhythm/conduction benchmark slice with 2,263 anonymized ECG records.

## Your Task
Build a multilabel classifier for rhythm and conduction findings from the staged WFDB ECG records.

## Input Files
- WFDB records directory: `ptbxl_2263\input\records`
- Required ECG ID list: `ptbxl_2263\input\record_ids.csv`
- Label glossary: `ptbxl_2263\input\label_codebook.csv`
- Output template: `ptbxl_2263\input\template_output.csv`

## Software
- Task-local command prompt helper: `ptbxl_2263\software\open_input_cmd.bat`
- Baseline package installer: `ptbxl_2263\software\install_baseline_python_packages.bat`
- You may use the system `python` on the VM and install additional open-source Python packages if needed

## What You Must Do
1. Read the staged ECG records from `ptbxl_2263\input\records`.
2. Use `ptbxl_2263\input\record_ids.csv` as the exact required output row set.
3. Train or fit any CPU-feasible multilabel workflow you judge appropriate.
4. Write one CSV exactly to:
   `ptbxl_2263\output\predictions.csv`

## Output Requirements
- The file must be named exactly `predictions.csv`
- The columns must be exactly:
  `ecg_id, SR, STACH, SBRAD, SARRH, AFIB, AFLT, PACE, CLBBB, CRBBB, LAFB, 1AVB, IRBBB, NORM`
- Include exactly the ECG IDs from `ptbxl_2263\input\record_ids.csv`
- Every label value must be binary: `0` or `1`
- Do not save extra files into `ptbxl_2263\output`

## Important Constraints
- Treat this as a multilabel problem; labels are not guaranteed to be mutually exclusive
- Use the staged task files as the source of truth for row set and schema
agent_must_do: Open the staged task directory on the Windows VM and inspect the ECG bundle under `input/`.

Load all 2,263 WFDB records from `input/records/` and build a multi-label classifier for the 13 labels `SR`, `STACH`, `SBRAD`, `SARRH`, `AFIB`, `AFLT`, `PACE`, `CLBBB`, `CRBBB`, `LAFB`, `1AVB`, `IRBBB`, and `NORM`.
Write `output/predictions.csv` with exactly the IDs from `input/record_ids.csv` and binary predictions for all 13 labels in the required order.

Make the modeling decisions needed to get there under CPU-only constraints, including waveform preprocessing, feature/model family, multilabel thresholding, and any class-imbalance handling; the benchmark contract does not prescribe a single fixed recipe.

input_files.description: 2,263 anonymized 12-lead, 500 Hz, 10 s ECGs

input_files.description: One-column CSV with header ecg_id; exact required output ID set

input_files.description: Two-column CSV label,description giving the public meaning of each target label

input_files.name: Output template
input_files.description: Canonical 14-column schema ecg_id plus the 13 label columns, with blank prediction cells and the required row order

rows.title: Prostate IMRT matRad Reproduction
rows.summary: Act as a senior medical physicist: reproduce a fixed-field prostate IMRT reference plan with matRad + GNU Octave on Linux, repair three planted RTSTRUCT defects, optimize fluence + Engel leaf sequencing, export a consistent DICOM-RT bundle, and produce independent Python QA artifacts.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a senior medical physicist performing an independent research replanning benchmark on a fixed-field prostate IMRT reference plan using matRad (open-source treatment planning) and GNU Octave on Linux.

Task directory:
- `base`

Visible inputs (do not modify):
- CT DICOM series: `base/input/dicom/CT`
- Corrupted RTSTRUCT (contains 3 planted defects): `base/input/dicom/RTSTRUCT.dcm`
- Prescription: `base/input/prescription.json`
- Institutional DVH constraints and margin recipe: `base/input/institutional_constraints.md`
- Beam geometry (7 gantry angles): `base/input/beam_geometry.json`
- matRad beam model: `base/input/machine/benchmark_6MV.mat`
- matRad plan template: `base/input/pln_template.mat`
- Agent-facing README: `base/input/README_AGENT.md`
- Repair recipe notes: `base/input/repair_recipes.md`
- Submission output template: `base/input/submission_template`
- File hashes: `base/input/manifest.json`
- matRad/Octave launcher (preinstalled): `base/software/run_matrad.sh`

Your task (six phases):
1. Structure QA: identify and fix three defects planted in the supplied RTSTRUCT (clinical-rule corrections described in `base/input/repair_recipes.md`).
2. Import into matRad using the shipped `base/input/pln_template.mat` and `base/input/machine/benchmark_6MV.mat` (7 coplanar 6 MV beams, Engel sequencing 7 levels, RNG seed 42).
3. Fluence optimization with Engel leaf sequencing. Naive weights violate the rectum V70Gy constraint; expect 3-6 weight-tuning iterations.
4. Deterministic pencil-beam (SVDPB) dose calculation at 3 mm grid.
5. DICOM-RT export of RTPLAN.dcm, RTDOSE.dcm, and corrected RTSTRUCT, all sharing a consistent FrameOfReferenceUID.
6. Independent QA in Python: recompute DVH from the submitted RTDOSE + RTSTRUCT, render axial/sagittal/coronal isodose PNGs, and produce `report.md`, `plan_metrics.json`, `beam_summary.csv`, `decisions.md`.

Required outputs, written only under `base/output`:
- `RTPLAN.dcm`, `RTDOSE.dcm`, `RTSTRUCT_corrected.dcm`
- `replay_state.mat` (numeric-only matRad state for independent replay)
- `dvh_metrics.csv`, `plan_metrics.json`, `beam_summary.csv`
- `figures/axial.png`, `figures/sagittal.png`, `figures/coronal.png` (each >= 800x800)
- `report.md`, `decisions.md`

Runtime guidance:
- Invoke matRad / Octave via `base/software/run_matrad.sh`; the wrapper activates the pinned `rtplan-matrad` environment (GNU Octave 6.4.0, matRad commit `c014dc82`, Python 3.10 with pydicom / pymedphys / numba / numpy / scipy / matplotlib / scikit-image).
- No network access is required after the environment is installed.
- Do not modify files under `input/`. Write the final bundle only under `base/output`.
agent_must_do: Repair the three planted RTSTRUCT defects (Rectum `RTROIInterpretedType = ORGAN`; derive `PTV_7800` by expanding the `PTV_placeholder` CTV with the institutional margin recipe; re-derive the clipped External contour from CT).
Import the clinical geometry into matRad using the shipped `pln_template.mat` + `benchmark_6MV.mat` with the 7 coplanar 6 MV beams, RNG seed 42, and Engel sequencing (7 levels).
Tune fluence weights (3–6 iterations) so rectum V70Gy ≤ 20% and the other institutional DVH constraints are met.
Run deterministic pencil-beam (SVDPB) dose calculation at the 3 mm grid.
Export `RTPLAN.dcm`, `RTDOSE.dcm`, and the corrected RTSTRUCT with consistent `FrameOfReferenceUID`, CT-aligned origin/spacing, and contour z-planes on CT slices.

Produce the independent Python QA bundle (`dvh_metrics.csv`, `plan_metrics.json`, `beam_summary.csv`, three ≥800×800 isodose PNGs, `report.md`, `decisions.md`) plus the numeric-only `replay_state.mat` in `output/`.

rows.title: SimGlucose Safe Basal Control
rows.summary: Implement a meal-unannounced, basal-only glucose controller for SimGlucose that satisfies safety gates across hidden patient episodes.
rows.task_prompt:
You are working on a Linux VM to implement a meal-unannounced basal-only glucose controller in SimGlucose.

Visible task files:
- Task brief: `base/input/public/task.md`
- Controller API: `base/input/public/task_api.py`
- Submission format: `base/input/public/submission_format.md`
- Public evaluator: `base/input/public/evaluate_public.py`
- Agent runtime manifest: `base/input/runtime_env/pyproject.toml`
- Agent runtime lockfile: `base/input/runtime_env/uv.lock`

Write your submission under `base/output/submission`.
Required files:
- `base/output/submission/controller.py`
- `base/output/submission/metadata.json`

Optional supporting files:
- `base/output/submission/report.md`
- `base/output/submission/assets/...`
- `base/output/submission/training_code/...`

Rules:
- Follow the public observation/action contract exactly.
- The controller must expose either `build_controller()` or `SubmissionController`.
- Use only the staged task files as your source of truth.
- If you need Python dependencies for solving, install them yourself from `base/input/runtime_env`.
agent_must_do: Read the staged public task package under input/public/ including the observation/action contract and submission format
Implement submission/controller.py exposing build_controller() or SubmissionController
Write submission/metadata.json with all required fields
Design a meal-unannounced, basal-only controller using only current CGM, time of day, sample interval, and action bounds
